title: 項莊舞劍
text:
項莊舞劍：貝森特真正在保衛的是日圓嗎？
官方說法是援助盟友。真正的誘因，是防止美國國債市場出現失控式拋售。



秦朝末年，各路起義軍中，劉邦與項羽的勢力最為強大。雙方曾約定：誰先攻下秦都咸陽，誰就在關中稱王。結果劉邦先入咸陽，項羽大怒。
項羽的遠房叔父項伯，與劉邦的謀士張良交情甚篤。聽到消息後，項伯連夜趕去警告張良，勸他趕緊逃走。張良不願拋棄主公，反而引薦劉邦與項伯相見。劉邦熱情接待，並與項伯結為兒女親家。項伯於是勸劉邦親自前往向項羽解釋、道歉。
翌日，劉邦率隨從抵達鴻門。項羽的首席謀士范增力勸主公在宴席上除掉劉邦，並埋伏武士，約定項羽舉杯為號即動手。
宴席上，劉邦態度謙卑、極盡奉承。項羽性情直爽，漸漸被安撫，不再有殺意，對范增多次示意皆視而不見。范增見計謀難成，便找來項羽的堂弟項莊，說：「大王太仁慈了。你進去以舞劍助興為名，趁機殺了劉邦。」
項莊入席敬酒後，請求舞劍。劍光閃動，越舞越靠近劉邦。項伯見狀著急，起身說：「一人獨舞興致不高，讓我來對舞吧！」隨即拔劍起舞，暗中以身體擋在劉邦身前，使項莊無法下手。
張良見情況危急，趕忙出去對劉邦的猛將樊噲說：「現在項莊拔劍起舞，他的用意就是要殺沛公啊！」這正是《史記》名句「今者項莊拔劍舞，其意常在沛公也」的由來。樊噲立即持武器闖入宴席。在張良與樊噲的保護下，劉邦最終找到機會離開，安全返回自己的軍營。
這就是歷史上著名的「鴻門宴」。
時光快轉兩千多年，場景換到華盛頓與東京。
美國財政部長斯科特•貝森特（Scott Bessent）剛剛與日本聯手，罕見地進行協調干預，以支撐持續暴跌的日圓。官方說法是盟友之間的團結之舉。日圓已跌至數十年低點，逼近1美元兌164日圓，為1980年代中期以來最弱水準。日圓此前處於無序貶值狀態，進口通脹（尤其是能源與民生必需品）上升，東京擔心日圓貶值陷入死亡螺旋。
表面上看，華盛頓的協助顯得慷慨。但若進一步以「誘因是塑造人類行為最強力的力量」這條公理來分析，整齣戲就像極了項莊舞劍：表面表演是一回事，真正的目標卻是另一回事。
干預真正的目標，是防止美國國債出現失控式拋售。
日本是美國國債最大的外國持有者，帳上約持有1.14至1.2兆美元。若東京為了捍衛日圓而大量拋售這些國債，將在美國長期殖利率本已敏感的時刻，進一步推高殖利率。貝森特絕不會讓這種情況發生。
干預日圓的邏輯十分明顯。日圓貶值會把通膨輸入日本。要支撐匯率，東京的選擇有限。若積極加息，將推高日本政府公債殖利率。日本債務對GDP比率超過200%，殖利率急升可能引發經濟衰退，並導致龐大的日圓套利交易（yen carry trade）無序平倉。
所謂日圓套利交易，是指借入低息日圓，投資於其他高收益資產，估計規模從數千億美元到數兆美元不等（若計入槓桿與不列入資產負債表的部份）。日圓若突然大幅升值，這些套利交易就被迫平倉，投資者必須賣掉外國資產（包括美國國債）來償還日圓借款，這是華盛頓最不想見到的情況。
日本的另一選擇是賣出自己擁有的美國國債換取美元，再用美元買入日圓。貝森特不允許這種情況發生，因此他推動擴大聯準會的「外國與國際貨幣當局回購機制」（FIMA Repo Facility）——目前每個交易對手每日上限為600億美元——讓日本能以國債作為抵押借入美元進行干預，而不必拋售美國債券。
在最近這次行動中，美國更進一步選擇賣出歐元（而非美元）來買入日圓。若賣出美元，將與「強勢美元」政策相矛盾，並可能進一步推高美國殖利率；賣出歐洲資產則無此顧慮。有報導指出，歐洲中央銀行是在交易完成後才被告知——這是違背主要央行之間慣常諮商規範的罕見做法。
市場的即時反應相當戲劇性：日圓在短時間內急漲約5%。日圓升勢持續了多久？數日後日圓就回吐相當部分漲幅，回落到1美元兌157至158日圓區間。歷史經驗顯示，這類干預多半只是爭取短暫喘息的時間，而非扭轉根本趨勢。利差、日本的財政軌跡，以及支撐日圓弱勢的結構性力量，基本上都還在。若日圓貶值再度加速，將需要更大規模、更頻繁的干預。
其他國家與大型機構也因各自理由（外匯儲備管理、流動性、收益率等）持有大量美國債務。一旦其中任何一方因為某種需要——例如為了取得美元購買石油——而決定賣出美國國債，同樣的壓力就會出現。華盛頓不願看到外國帳戶在市場已承壓時拋售美國國債，這將迫使貝森特發動越來越多此類干預。而這些干預，本質上不過是用憑空印出的美元，進行變相的收益率曲線控制。
簡言之，為了不讓美國長期國債殖利率升得太高、太快，貝森特會用盡一切可用方法以及任何必要手段，阻止美國國債泡沫爆破。
債券市場的損失，將被轉移到貨幣層面，也就是我們口袋裡的銀紙購買力會不斷下降。
對投資人而言，自保之路是黃金與白銀。
項莊舞劍，嘴上說只是助興。真正的意圖，從來不是助興。今天也一樣。跟著誘因走，真正目的就清楚了。

title: Xiang Zhuang’s Sword Dance
text:
Xiang Zhuang’s Sword Dance(项庄舞剑): Why Bessent Is Really Defending the Yen
The official story is helping an ally. The real incentive is protecting the U.S. Treasury market from a disorderly unwind.



In the dying days of the Qin Dynasty (秦朝) in ancient China, two great rebel armies stood out: Liu Bang’s (刘邦) and Xiang Yu’s (项羽). They had agreed that whoever first took the Qin capital of Xianyang (咸阳) would become king in the Guanzhong (关中) region. Liu Bang got there first. Xiang Yu was furious.
Xiang Yu’s distant uncle, Xiang Bo (项伯), was a close friend of Liu Bang’s strategist Zhang Liang (张良). Hearing of the danger, Xiang Bo raced overnight to warn Zhang Liang and urge him to flee. Zhang Liang refused to abandon his lord. Instead he arranged an introduction; Liu Bang received Xiang Bo warmly and even sealed a marriage alliance between their families. Xiang Bo then advised Liu Bang to go in person and apologize.
The next day Liu Bang arrived at Hongmen (鸿门) with his men. Xiang Yu’s chief adviser, Fan Zeng (范增), urged his master to kill Liu Bang during the banquet. Armed men were hidden nearby; the signal would be Xiang Yu raising his cup.
At the feast Liu Bang was all humility and flattery. Xiang Yu, a blunt and straightforward man, was gradually soothed and lost interest in the assassination. He ignored Fan Zeng’s repeated signals. Frustrated, Fan Zeng summoned Xiang Yu’s cousin Xiang Zhuang (项庄): “The king is too soft-hearted. Go in under the pretext of a sword dance and kill Liu Bang when the chance comes.”
Xiang Zhuang entered, offered a toast, and began to dance with his sword, the blade flashing ever closer to Liu Bang. Alarmed, Xiang Bo rose and said, “One man dancing alone is dull - let me join him!” He too drew his sword and danced, deliberately shielding Liu Bang so that Xiang Zhuang could find no opening.
Zhang Liang slipped outside and told Liu Bang’s fierce general Fan Kuai (樊哙): “Xiang Zhuang is dancing with his sword - his real intent is to kill Pei Gong!” (This is the origin of the famous line from the Records of the Grand Historian: “Xiang Zhuang drew his sword and danced, his mind always on Pei Gong. (沛公)” 《史记》:「今者项庄拔剑舞，其意常在沛公也」 ) Fan Kuai burst in fully armed. Under the protection of Zhang Liang and Fan Kuai, Liu Bang eventually returned safely to his own camp.
That is the celebrated story of the Hongmen Banquet (鸿门宴).
Now fast-forward a couple of thousand years to Washington and Tokyo.
U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has just joined Japan in a rare coordinated intervention to prop up the plunging yen. Officially it is an act of alliance solidarity - helping a friend whose currency had slid to multi-decade lows near 164 yen to the dollar, levels not seen since the mid-1980s. The yen had been in a disorderly decline; imported inflation (especially energy and daily necessities) was rising; and Tokyo feared a death spiral.
On the surface, Washington’s help looks generous. Dig a little deeper by analyzing incentives that are the strongest forces that shape human behavior, it becomes clear that the whole melodrama starts to resemble Xiang Zhuang’s sword dance: the visible performance is one thing; the real target is something else entirely.
The real target is the U.S. Treasury market.
Japan is the largest foreign holder of U.S. Treasuries, with roughly $1.14–1.2 trillion on its books. A disorderly yen defense by Tokyo that involved heavy selling of those Treasuries would push U.S. long-term yields higher at a moment when they are already sensitive. Bessent will not let that happen.
The yen death spiral is straightforward but unpleasant. A weaker yen imports inflation into Japan. To support the currency, Tokyo has limited options. Raising interest rates more aggressively would push Japanese government bond yields higher. With Japan’s debt-to-GDP ratio still north of 200 percent, a sharp rise in yields risks recession and a disorderly unwind of the vast yen carry trade.
That carry trade - borrowing cheap yen to invest in higher-yielding assets elsewhere - has been estimated in recent years anywhere from several hundred billion to multiple trillions of dollars in notional exposure once leverage and off-balance-sheet positions are considered. An abrupt strengthening of the yen forces those positions to be closed: investors sell the foreign assets (including U.S. Treasuries) to repay the yen loans. The result is selling pressure on the very market Washington most wants to keep orderly.
The alternative for Japan is to sell its existing stock of U.S. Treasuries for dollars and then buy yen. That, of course, is precisely the outcome Bessent is determined to avoid. Hence the push to expand the Federal Reserve’s Foreign and International Monetary Authorities (FIMA) Repo Facility - currently capped at $60 billion per counter party per day - so that Japan can post Treasuries as collateral, borrow dollars, and intervene without dumping the bonds into the open market.
In the recent operation the United States went a step further and sold euros (rather than dollars) to buy yen. Selling dollars would have contradicted the stated strong-dollar policy and risked further upward pressure on U.S. yields. Selling a European asset did not. Reports indicate the European Central Bank was informed only after the trades had settled - an unusual breach of the usual consultation norms among major central banks.
The immediate market effect was dramatic: the yen spiked roughly five percent in short order. How long did the fireworks last? Not long. Within days the currency had given back a substantial portion of the gains and drifted back toward the 157–158 range. History suggests these interventions buy time rather than reverse the underlying trend. The interest-rate differential, Japan’s fiscal trajectory, and the structural forces behind yen weakness remain largely intact. Larger and more frequent interventions will be required if the slide resumes.
Other countries and large institutions also hold substantial amounts of U.S. debt for their own reasons - reserve management, liquidity, yield… Should any of them decide, for whatever reasons, like they need to sell Treasuries to get US dollars to buy oil, the same pressure appears. Washington’s reluctance to see foreign accounts sell Treasuries into a stressed market will require Bessent to initiate more and more such interventions, and all these interventions are nothing but yield curve control using dollars printed out of thin air.
In short, to keep long-term Treasury yields from rising too far or too fast, Bessent will explore every available route - FIMA expansion, creative use of euro reserves, joint intervention rhetoric, whatever it takes.
Losses in the bond market will be shifted, as far as possible, into the currency. In other words, the purchasing power of the money in our pockets will steadily decline.
For investors, the escape route is gold and silver.
Xiang Zhuang danced with the sword and claimed it was only entertainment. The real intent was never the entertainment. The same principle applies today. Follow the incentives, and the motive becomes clear.

title: 美联储动辄得咎
text:
横又死，掂又死：美联储动辄得咎，在所难免
联储局主席凯文•沃什无论选择哪条路，黄金都会胜出



在荷马的《奥德赛》中，英雄奥德修斯必须驾船穿越一条狭窄的海峡，两侧各有致命危险。一边是斯库拉（Scylla），一头有六颗脑袋的怪物，会从甲板上把水手抓走；另一边是卡律布狄斯（Charybdis），一个巨大的漩涡，能把整艘船吞没。女巫喀耳刻（Circe）建议他靠近斯库拉航行，牺牲少数水手，也不要冒着整艘船被漩涡吞噬的风险。奥德修斯无奈照做，六名船员丧命，船却得以幸存。
新任联储局主席凯文•沃什（Kevin Warsh）正处于同样的海峡之中。一边是大幅加息以压制通胀；另一边是维持低利率（或只小幅加息），任由通膨继续侵蚀货币购买力。两条路都系死路一条。唯一的问题是：他愿意承受哪一种痛苦。
抑制通胀的直接办法向来是提高利率。高利率会冷却需求、支撑美元，最终让物价受控。但美国身子虚弱，已不再是一个担受得起这种经典疗法的国家。目前全国总债务接近 39.8 兆美元，并有望在数月内突破 40 兆美元。本财年年度赤字接近 1.9 兆美元，且看不出有缩小的迹象。单是社会保障（Social Security）与联邦医疗保险（Medicare）就占联邦预算极大比例 - 社会保障约占支出的 22–23%，联邦医疗保险另占 14–17%。如今净利息支出已相当于或什至超过国防支出，并正朝每年超过 1 兆美元攀升。这些项目在政治上几乎不可触碰，尤其在中期选举逼近之际。削减福利等于政治自杀。
加息也会重创股市。美国经济高度依赖消费，而家庭财富以及消费信心与股价紧密相连。资本利得及相关税收构成联邦收入中不可忽视的一部分。股市若持续下跌，这些收入会缩水，同时利息成本却在上升，进一步令财政状况恶化。
然后是债券市场，真正的「房间里的大象」。股市或许抢占新闻头条，但真正为政府融资的是美国公债市场。目前流通的美国公债已超过 30 兆美元；更广泛的美国债券市场规模更大。长期殖利率上升会威胁整个国家的融资机制。当 10 年期美债殖利率从 2026 年 2 月底约 3.97% 升至现在 4.6% 或什至更高时，政府（以及所有其他人）的借贷成本已明显上升。如果沃什加息到足以杀死通胀的程度，将可能引发通缩式崩溃，而在目前的债务对 GDP 比率下，这在政治与经济上都不可接受。物价与收入下跌会提高现有债务的实质负担，触发连锁违约，并可能陷入自我强化的债务通缩螺旋，政府与央行不会长期容忍这种局面。历史上政府对这类威胁的回应，一向是大规模注入流动性、财政刺激与货币扩张 - 而这正是黄金历来蓬勃发展的环境。
沃什几乎没有真正的选择。像之前的主席一样，他必须继续做不可持续的事，才能让不可持续的局面再维持一阵子。在一个接近 40 兆美元债务、结构性庞大赤字、以及政治上被视为神圣不可侵犯的社会福利的世界里，阻力最小的路径就是容忍较高通胀与较弱美元。
沃什就像奥德修斯一样，似乎选择了伤害较小的那条路：牺牲少数水手（接受较高通胀与弱美元），也不愿冒整艘船沉没的风险（债券市场爆破，迫使实施收益率曲线控制或其他更糟措施）。在最近的记者会上，他对物价稳定说得强硬，却选择维持利率不变。市场的反应显示长期殖利率将进一步走高，联准会最终会优先考虑金融稳定而非通胀。
我们正看着一位现代奥德修斯，决定要把哪些水手喂给怪物。船或许能勉强穿过海峡，但最有可能安全抵达彼岸，是那些持有真实资产、而非纸上承诺的投资者。

title: 貨幣雙重思想
text:
貨幣領域的「雙重思想」：戰爭即和平，黃金即垃圾



在喬治·奧威爾的1949年小說《1984》中，大洋國政府強迫公民接受“雙重思想”：即同時持有兩種相互矛盾的信念，並視兩者皆為真理，例如：“戰爭即和平”，“自由即奴役”，“無知即力量”等，其目的不僅僅是令人民服從，而是發自內心的深信不疑。人們必須感受這些口號就是現實，即使所有證據都指向相反的方向。
快進到2026年，金融市場已形成了一套屬於自己的“貨幣雙重思想”：“戰爭是通縮的”、“賣出黃金是避險”、“經濟數據糟糕對股市是利好的” … 投資者對此深信不疑，並以此為行事依據；黃金和白銀的表現印证了這一點，它們的走勢與歷史典籍、教科書以及常識的預測截然相反。
以下事件不斷循環發生：川普總統威脅要轟炸伊朗的橋樑、發電廠或石油基礎設施。市場因擔心石油衝擊而恐慌，原油價格飆升，通膨擔憂重燃。交易員紛紛押注升息，金銀遭到拋售。一兩天后，川普便上演了「TACO」把戲（TACO代表Trump Always Chickens Out，是華爾街的一個縮寫詞，意為「川普總是臨陣退縮」 - 指他慣於發出極端威脅語句，隨後又收回成命的行徑）。談判重啟，油價回落，升息憂慮緩解，貴金屬收復部分失地。隨後，循環重新開始。我們就像電影《偷天情緣》裡的比爾·默瑞一樣，被困在這個循環中已長達數月。
官方的解釋聽起來合乎邏輯：局勢升級推高了能源價格風險，進而推高CPI，迫使聯準會加息；而黃金是不產生收益的資產，美元收益率上升提高了其機會成本。因此黃金以美元計價下跌。白銀具有工業屬性，波動性更大，跌幅更深。當「TACO」時刻到來，持續油價衝擊的威脅消退，貴金屬就會反彈。完美的解釋。
然而，戰爭產生通膨，歷來如此。戰爭會破壞供應、資源被轉移、擴大赤字，並往往以印鈔收場。看看歷史數據便知：第一次世界大戰引發的通膨導緻美國物價上漲超過一倍，歐洲的情況更為嚴重。第二次世界大戰帶來了物資短缺和配給制；戰後一旦管制解除，美國物價在一年內飆升了20%以上。越戰主要依靠赤字而非稅收來提供資金，這助長了20世紀70年代的「大通膨」。1973年的贖罪日戰爭（第四次中東戰爭）及隨後的石油禁運導致原油價格翻了四倍，並引發了長達十年的滯脹。即使是規模較小的1990-1991年海灣戰爭，也導致了油價飆升和通膨率的顯著上升。追溯一個多世紀的地緣政治經濟指數顯示出同樣的規律：戰爭及戰爭威脅往往預示著軍費開支增加、債務攀升、貨幣貶值，進而導致通膨加劇！
可是我們現在卻將戰爭視為通貨緊縮因素，而非結構性的通膨推手。在金融與政治的世界裡，有時需要具備瘋子的視角，才能理解這種集體瘋狂現象：大眾正在拋售貴金屬，而貴金屬在歷史上恰恰能在政府發動戰爭並印鈔填補缺口時，有效保護購買力！
那些認為當前戰爭不利於黃金和白銀的投資者犯了大錯。聰明的資本往往透過反向押注大眾的錯誤假設來獲利。貴金屬價格先前已為「升息恐慌」的論調付出了代價：白銀價格已從2026年1月每盎司121美元的歷史高點腰斬；黃金價格也從約5500美元的峰值回落，跌去了約四分之一到三分之一的價值。然而，支撐其價格的基本驅動因素 - 持續的赤字、央行購金、白銀的工業需求以及法幣購買力的長期縮水- 仍然穩固。
當戰火最終平息，或者當市場終於明白戰爭具有通膨而非通縮效應時，貴金屬價格應該會重拾升勢。
戰爭引發通膨，黃金白銀提供保護。除此之外的一切，皆為「雙重思想」下的謬論。

title: Monetary Doublethink
text:
Monetary Doublethink: War Is Peace, Gold Is Trash



In George Orwell’s 1949 novel 1984, the Oceania Government forces citizens into Doublethink: the ability to hold two contradictory beliefs at the same time and accept both as true. “War is Peace.” “Freedom is Slavery.” “Ignorance is Strength.” The goal is not mere compliance, but genuine belief. People must feel the slogans as reality, even as the evidence screams otherwise.
Fast-forward to 2026, the financial markets have perfected their own version of Monetary Doublethink: “War is Deflationary”, “Selling gold is risk-off”, “Bad economic data is bullish for stocks” … Investors recite these lines with solemn conviction, as evidenced by gold and silver performing the opposite of what every history book, every textbook, and common sense would predict.
Watch the pattern. President Trump threatens to bomb Iranian bridges, power plants, or oil infrastructure. Markets panic over oil shocks. Crude spikes. Inflation fears reignite. Traders pile into rate-hike bets. Gold and silver get dumped. The next day or two, Trump “TACOs” (Trump Always Chickens Out, the Wall Street acronym for his well-documented habit of issuing maximalist threats and then walking them back). Talks resume. Oil softens. Rate fears ease. The metals claw back some of the losses. Then the loop resets. We have been stuck in this cycle for months, like Bill Murray in the movie “Groundhog Day”.
The official explanation sounds logical. Escalation raises the risk of higher energy prices, which would push CPI higher, which would force the Fed to hike rates. Gold pays no yield. Higher dollar yields raise its opportunity cost. Therefore gold falls in dollar terms. Silver, more industrial and more volatile, falls harder. When the TACO arrives and the threat of sustained oil spikes recedes, the metals recover. Perfect.
But war is inflationary. Always has been. Wars destroy supply, divert resources, expand deficits, and usually end in money printing. Look at the data. World War I produced inflation that more than doubled prices in the United States and far worse in Europe. World War II brought shortages, rationing, and a postwar surge that saw U.S. prices jump more than 20% in a single year once controls were lifted. The Vietnam War, financed by deficits rather than taxes, helped fuel the Great Inflation of the 1970s. The 1973 Yom Kippur War and subsequent oil embargo quadrupled crude prices and locked in a decade of stagflation. Even the more limited Gulf War of 1990–91 delivered an oil spike and a measurable inflation jump. Financial indices going back more than a century show the same pattern: wars and the threat of wars reliably foreshadow higher military spending, higher debt, currency debasement, and therefore higher inflation!
Yet here we are, treating war as deflationary rather than a structural inflationary force. In the world of money and politics, one sometimes needs the perspective of a lunatic to make sense of the collective madness. The crowd is selling the very asset that has historically protected purchasing power when governments go to war and print the difference.
Investors who treat the current war as harmful to gold and silver are making a big mistake. Clever capital profits precisely by positioning against the crowd’s erroneous assumption. The metals have already paid the price for the “rate-hike fear” narrative. Silver has roughly halved from its January 2026 all-time high of $121 per ounce. Gold has surrendered about a quarter to a third of its value from the peak around $5,500. Yet the underlying drivers - persistent deficits, central-bank buying, industrial demand for silver, and the long-term erosion of fiat purchasing power - remain intact.
When the shooting finally stops, or when the market finally understands that wars are inflationary rather than deflationary, the metals should reprice higher.
War inflates. Gold and silver protect. Everything else is Doublethink.

title: 谁是受益者？
text:
Cui Bono：为何凯文·沃什只是另一只伪装的鸽子



让我们从古罗马的一则小故事开始。当一位元老院议员在广场上被发现遇刺身亡时，伟大的演说家西塞罗会向群众提问：「Cui bono?」- 这对谁有利？谁是受益者？这个简单的问题往往比任何调查都更快揭开真相。两千年后的今天，同一提问依然跟灯塔的光芒一样，引导我们明白现代货币政策的底蕴。利益分配 - 而非新闻发布会上的华丽但空洞的词藻 - 才真正揭示人类行为的背后真相。
公理 1：Cui bono - 这对谁有利？ 
这是我在这些文章中将经常运用的第一原则。利益激励不仅包括物质上的丰厚薪酬和奖金，还包括「感觉良好」和「做正确的事」的心理满足感。
2026 年 6 月 17 日，凯文·沃什作为新任联储局主席举行了首次记者会。他郑重宣示致力于恢复物价稳定。最近2026年5月的通膨数据年增率升至4.2%，是三年多高位，主要受地缘政治冲突引发的能源价格暴涨所推动。然而，联储局却决定维持利率不变。
评论家们赞叹道：「沃什不一样！他是真正的鹰派！」
但我不敢苟同。
让我们利用益激励因素来分析吧。川普总统是低利率的爱好者。他公开宣称：「我爱通膨……那些数字很棒。你知道我真正爱什么吗？我爱通膨。」因为鲍威尔不肯积极大幅降息，川普猛烈抨击前主席鲍威尔行动太慢、是「彻底的失败者」和不懂变通。他把鲍威尔赶走，正是因为这位前主席不愿在中期选举前用宽松货币政策刺激经济。
川普会任命一位真正的抗通膨战士，甘冒经济放缓风险而大幅加息的人做联储局主席吗？当然不会。沃什得到这个职位，正是因为他会迎合川普的偏好。他只是表面强硬，但实际上会推行宽松货币政策。
想真正击败通膨，需要提高利率并减少印钞。就这么简单。但沃什却以能源供应冲击、AI可带来的生产力大幅提升，以及「需要更多证据」或更好数据作为借口，宣布成立多个工作小组来「检讨」联储局沟通方式、资产负债表、通膨框架等等典型的官僚拖延战术，继续量寛政策。
若沃什大幅推升联邦基金利率，将会让美国庞大国债的利息支出爆炸性增长。目前净利息支付已消耗联邦收入的约18–22%。利率若再升高，这一负担可能膨胀至收入的25%以上，排挤其他所有支出。在政治和财政上，这无异于自杀。因此，最有可能的政策方向是宽松。
沃什或许会小幅加息，以对抗持续走高的通膨，但实质利率几乎肯定仍会维持负值。更重要的是，一旦出现任何经济麻烦的迹象- 股市下挫、就业数据下滑，或是来自白宫的政治压力 - 他就会立刻煞车，毫不犹豫地降息。毕竟，关键时刻，利益高于一切。
被视为鹰派沃什的首次亮相（点阵图亦暗示可能升息），最初确实支撑了美元并压低股市 - 标普500指数当天下跌超过1%，成为数十年来新主席首次联邦公开市场委员会会议日表现最差之一。黄金与白银则在恐慌中被压低至接近200日移动平均线附近。但如果这种鹰派姿态只是表演，剧本就很清楚了：货币将持续贬值、美元长期走弱，以及贵金属作为可靠避风港会继续上涨。
投资者应考虑黄金和白银等硬资产，作为对抗长期货币贬值的保护。目前两种金属在卖压后正测试其200日移动平均线，这可能是一个好的买入机会。

這是我的第一篇文章！
「如果你想成為作家，那就付諸行動去寫。」— 愛比克泰德 (‘If you wish to be a writer, write.’ … Epictetus)
我一直想基於一些不言自明的公理，來探討邏輯與批判性思維，並用這些公理分析一般人類行為，尤其是經濟學和金融投資領域的行為。我希望這種方法能幫助投資人做出明智的投資決策。我拖延了很久，直到最近偶然讀到愛比克泰德的這句名言，終於決定付諸行動。
我希望能建立一個由志同道合者組成的社群，讓大家訂閱我的文章，並透過回饋互相促進、共同成長。
我的計劃是每週發布一到兩篇文章。

title: My First Post
text:
This is my first post!
‘If you wish to be a writer, write.’ … Epictetus
I always want to write about logical and critical thinking based on some self-evident axioms, and use these axioms to analyse human behaviour in general, and economics and financial investments in particular, and hopefully the approach would lead me to make sound investment decisions. I have procrastinated for a long time until very recently, I came across the above Epictetus quote, and finally decided to give it a go.
I would hope that I can start a community of like-minded people to subscribe to my blog, and obtain feedback for mutual improvement and satisfaction.
My plan is to post one or two pieces each week.

title: Cui Bono?
text:
Cui Bono: Why Kevin Warsh Is Just Another Dove in Disguise



Let us begin with a little tale from ancient Rome. When a senator was found murdered in the Forum, the great orator Cicero would ask the crowd: Cui bono? — To whom is it a benefit? Who gains? This simple question often unraveled the truth faster than any forensic sleuthing. Fast-forward a couple of millennia, and the same axiom shines like a beacon in the fog of mysterious monetary policy. Incentives, not press-conference mere rhetoric, reveal the truth about human behavior.
Axiom 1: Cui bono — to whom is it a benefit?
This is the first principle I’ll wield frequently in these postings. Incentives include not just material rewards like fat paychecks and bonuses, but also the psychological satisfaction of “feeling good” and “doing the right thing”.
On June 17, 2026, Kevin Warsh held his first press conference as the new Fed Chairman. He professed a solemn commitment to restoring price stability. Recent inflation? A stubborn 4.2% year-over-year in May 2026 — the highest in over three years, driven largely by surging energy prices amid geopolitical fireworks. Yet the Fed left interest rates unchanged.
Pundits swooned: “Warsh is different! A real hawk!”
I beg to differ.
Let’s follow the incentives, shall we? President Trump is a low-interest-rate guy. He openly declared, “I love the inflation… The numbers were great. You know what I really love? I love the inflation.” Trump hammered prior Chair Jerome Powell as “Mr. Too Late,” a “major loser,” and a “real stiff” for not slashing rates aggressively enough. He pushed Powell aside precisely because the old chair wouldn’t goose the economy with easy money ahead of the midterms.
Would Trump appoint a genuine inflation warrior who’d hike rates and risk a slowdown? Of course not. Warsh got the job because the incentives align. He will talk tough but deliver accommodation. Pretend hawkishness is the perfect cover.
Truly slaying inflation requires higher rates and less money printing. Simple as that. Instead, Warsh offered excuses centered on supply shocks (energy, etc.), productivity hopes (thanks to AI), and the need for “more evidence” or better data. He announced task forces to “review” communications, the balance sheet, inflation frameworks, and more — classic bureaucratic delay tactics while the printing press stays warm.
Pushing the fed funds rate meaningfully higher would explode interest costs on the US gargantuan national debt, not to mention risking Trump’s mid-term election. Net interest payments already consume roughly 18–22% of federal revenues. At higher rates, that burden could balloon toward 25%+ of revenue, crowding out everything else. Politically and financially suicidal it is. So incentives says the most likely way forward is continued accommodation and money printing.
Warsh may raise rates modestly to fight inflation if the latter continues to go higher, but real interest rates would almost certainly remain negative. More importantly, the moment there’s even the slightest hint of economic trouble — a wobble in the stock market, a dip in employment, or political pressure from the White House — he will slam on the brakes and cut rates without hesitation. After all, when push comes to shove, the incentives always win.
Warsh’s perceived hawkish debut (with the dot plot hinting at possible hikes) initially strengthened the dollar and pressured stocks — the S&P 500 dropped over 1% that day, marking one of the worst first-Fed-day performances in decades. Gold and silver were slammed toward their 200-day moving averages amid the scare. But if this hawkishness is mostly theater (as incentives strongly suggest), the long-term script is clear: persistent currency debasement, a weaker U.S. Dollar over time, and higher precious metals as the reliable escape hatch.
Investors would do well to consider hard assets like gold and silver as protection against long-term currency debasement. With both metals recently testing their 200-day moving averages after the selloff, this could turn out to be a compelling buying opportunity.

title: 誰是受益者？
text:
Cui Bono：為何凱文·沃什只是另一隻偽裝的鴿子



讓我們從古羅馬的一則小故事開始。當一位元老院議員在廣場上被發現遇刺身亡時，偉大的演說家西塞羅會向群眾提問：「Cui bono?」- 這對誰有利？誰是受益者？這個簡單的問題往往比任何調查都更快揭開真相。兩千年後的今天，同一提問依然跟燈塔的光芒一樣，引導我們明白現代貨幣政策的底蘊。利益分配 - 而非新聞發布會上的華麗但空洞的詞藻 - 才真正揭示人類行為的背後真相。
公理 1：Cui bono - 這對誰有利？
這是我在這些文章中將經常運用的第一原則。利益激勵不僅包括物質上的豐厚薪酬和獎金，還包括「感覺良好」和「做正確的事」的心理滿足感。
2026 年 6 月 17 日，凱文·沃什作為新任聯儲局主席舉行了首次記者會。他鄭重宣示致力於恢復物價穩定。最近2026年5月的通膨數據年增率升至4.2%，是三年多高位，主要受地緣政治衝突引發的能源價格暴漲所推動。然而，聯儲局卻決定維持利率不變。
評論家們讚歎道：「沃什不一樣！他是真正的鷹派！」
但我不敢苟同。
讓我們用利益激勵因素來分析吧。川普總統是低利率的愛好者。他公開宣稱：「我愛通膨……那些數字很棒。你知道我真正愛什麼嗎？我愛通膨。」因為鮑威爾不肯積極大幅降息，川普猛烈抨擊前主席鮑威爾行動太慢、是「徹底的失敗者」和不懂變通。他把鮑威爾趕走，正是因為這位前主席不願在中期選舉前用寬鬆貨幣政策刺激經濟。
川普會任命一位真正的抗通膨戰士，甘冒經濟放緩風險而大幅加息的人做聯儲局主席嗎？當然不會。沃什得到這個職位，正是因為他會迎合川普的偏好。他只是表面強硬，但實際上會推行寬鬆貨幣政策。
想真正擊敗通膨，需要提高利率並減少印鈔。就這麼簡單。但沃什卻以能源供應衝擊、AI可帶來的生產力大幅提升，以及「需要更多證據」或更好數據作為藉口，宣布成立多個工作小組來「檢討」聯儲局溝通方式、資產負債表、通膨框架等等典型的官僚拖延戰術，繼續量寛政策。
若沃什大幅推升聯邦基金利率，將會讓美國龐大國債的利息支出爆炸性增長。目前淨利息支付已消耗聯邦收入的約18–22%。利率若再升高，這 - 負擔可能膨脹至收入的25%以上，排擠其他所有支出。在政治和財政上，這無異於自殺。因此，最有可能的政策方向是寬鬆。
沃什或許會小幅加息，以對抗持續走高的通膨，但實質利率幾乎肯定仍會維持負值。更重要的是，一旦出現任何經濟麻煩的跡象- 股市下挫、就業數據下滑，或是來自白宮的政治壓力 - 他就會立刻煞車，毫不猶豫地降息。畢竟，關鍵時刻，利益高於一切。
被視為鷹派沃什的首次亮相（點陣圖亦暗示可能升息），最初確實支撐了美元並壓低股市 - 標普500指數當天下跌超過1%，成為數十年來新主席首次聯邦公開市場委員會會議日表現最差之一。黃金與白銀則在恐慌中被壓低至接近200日移動平均線附近。但如果這種鷹派姿態只是表演，劇本就很清楚了：貨幣將持續貶值、美元長期走弱，以及貴金屬作為可靠避風港會繼續上漲。
投資者應考慮黃金和白銀等硬資產，作為對抗長期貨幣貶值的保護。目前兩種金屬在賣壓後正測試其200日移動平均線，這可能是一個好的買入機會。

title: 货币双重思想
text:
货币领域的「双重思想」：战争即和平，黄金即垃圾



在乔治·奥威尔的1949年小说《1984》中，大洋国政府强迫公民接受“双重思想”：即同时持有两种相互矛盾的信念，并视两者皆为真理，例如：“战争即和平”，“自由即奴役”，“无知即力量”等，其目的不仅仅是令人民服从，而是发自内心的深信不疑。人们必须感受这些口号就是现实，即使所有证据都指向相反的方向。
快进到2026年，金融市场已形成了一套屬於自己的”貨幣双重思想”：“战争是通缩的”、“卖出黄金是避险”、“经济数据糟糕对股市是利好的” … 投资者對此深信不疑，並以此為行事依据；黄金和白银的表现印征了這一点，它們的走勢與歷史典籍、教科书以及常识的预测截然相反。
以下事件不斷循环發生：特朗普总统威胁要轰炸伊朗的桥梁、发电厂或石油基础设施。市场因担心石油冲击而恐慌，原油价格飙升，通胀担忧重燃。交易员纷纷押注加息，金银遭到抛售。一两天后，特朗普便上演了“TACO”把戏（TACO代表Trump Always Chickens Out，是华尔街的一个缩写词，意为“特朗普总是临阵退缩” - 指他惯于发出极端威胁語句，随后又收回成命的行径）。谈判重启，油价回落，加息忧虑缓解，贵金属收复部分失地。随后，循环重新开始。我们就像电影《偷天情缘》里的比尔·默瑞一样，被困在这个循环中已长达数月。
官方的解释听起来合乎逻辑：局势升级推高了能源价格风险，进而推高CPI，迫使美联储加息；而黄金是不产生收益的资产，美元收益率上升提高了其机会成本。因此黄金以美元计价下跌。白银具工业属性，波动性更大，跌幅更深。当“TACO”时刻到来，持续油价冲击的威胁消退，贵金属就会反弹。完美的解释。
然而，战争產生通胀，历来如此。战争会破坏供应、资源被转移、扩大赤字，并往往以印钞收场。看看历史数据便知：第一次世界大战引发的通胀导致美国物价上漲超過一倍，欧洲的情况则更为严重。第二次世界大战带来了物资短缺和配给制；战后一旦管制解除，美国物价在一年内便飙升了20%以上。越南战争主要依靠赤字而非税收来提供资金，这助长了20世纪70年代的“大通胀”。1973年的赎罪日战争（第四次中东战争）及随后的石油禁运导致原油价格翻了四倍，并引发了长达十年的滞胀。即使是规模较小的1990-1991年海湾战争，也导致了油价飙升和通胀率的明显上升。追溯一个多世纪的地缘政治经济指数显示出同样的规律：战争及战争威胁往往预示着军费开支增加、债务攀升、货币贬值，进而导致通胀加剧！
可是我们现在却将战争视为通缩因素，而非结构性的通胀推手。在金融与政治的世界里，有时需要具备疯子的视角，才能理解这种集体疯狂现象：大众正在抛售贵金属，而贵金属在历史上恰恰能在政府发动战争并印钞填补缺口时，有效保护购买力！
那些认为当前战争不利于黄金和白银的投资者犯了大错。聪明的资本往往通过反向押注大众的错误假设来获利。贵金属价格此前已为“加息恐慌”的论调付出了代价：白银价格已从2026年1月每盎司121美元的历史高点腰斩；黄金价格也从约5500美元的峰值回落，跌去了约四分之一到三分之一的价值。然而，支撑其价格的基本驱动因素 - 持续的赤字、央行购金、白银的工业需求以及法币购买力的长期缩水- 依然稳固。
当战火最终平息，或者当市场终于明白战争具有通胀而非通缩效应时，贵金属价格應該會重拾升势。
战争引发通胀，黄金白银提供保护。除此之外的一切，皆为“双重思想”下的谬论。

title: Kevin Warsh’s Impossible Choice
text:
Between Scylla and Charybdis: Kevin Warsh’s Impossible Choice
Why the Fed chairman has no good options left, and why gold wins either way



In Homer’s Odyssey, the hero Odysseus must sail his ship through a narrow strait guarded by two mortal dangers. On one side lurks Scylla, a six-headed monster that snatches sailors from the deck. On the other spins Charybdis, a giant whirlpool that can swallow the entire vessel. Circe advises him to steer closer to Scylla and sacrifice a few men rather than risk losing everything to the whirlpool. Odysseus reluctantly complies. Six crew members die. The ship survives.
Kevin Warsh, the new Federal Reserve chairman, finds himself in the same strait. On one side: raise interest rates aggressively enough to crush inflation. On the other: keep rates low (or raise them only modestly) and let inflation continue to erode the currency. There is no clean passage. Both paths inflict damage. The only question is which damage he is willing to accept.
The straightforward remedy for inflation has always been higher rates. Higher rates cool demand, strengthen the dollar, and eventually bring prices under control. But the United States is no longer a country that can afford the classic cure. Gross national debt stands near USD 39.8 trillion and is on track to cross USD 40 trillion within months. Annual deficits are running close to USD 1.9 trillion this fiscal year and show little sign of shrinking. Social Security and Medicare alone consume enormous shares of the federal budget: Social Security roughly 22–23 percent of outlays and Medicare another 14–17 percent, with net interest payments now rivaling or exceeding defense spending and climbing past USD 1 trillion a year. These programs are politically untouchable, especially with midterm elections approaching. Cutting them would be electoral suicide.
A rate hike would also hammer the stock market. The U.S. economy is heavily consumption-driven, and household wealth (and the confidence that fuels spending) is tied tightly to equity prices. Capital-gains and related tax receipts form a meaningful portion of federal revenue. A sustained market decline would shrink those receipts just as interest costs rise - an ugly combination that further worsens the fiscal situation.
Then there is the bond market, the true elephant in the room. The stock market may capture the headlines, but the Treasury market is where the government actually funds itself. Outstanding Treasury debt already exceed USD30 trillion; the broader U.S. bond market is larger still. A rise in long-term yields threatens the entire financing mechanism of the state. When the 10-year Treasury yield climbed from about 3.97 percent in late February 2026 to the mid-4.6 percent range and beyond, borrowing costs for the government (and for everyone else) rose materially. If Warsh raises rates sufficiently high enough to kill inflation, it will cause a deflationary collapse that is politically and economically unacceptable at current debt-to-GDP ratios. Falling prices and incomes would raise the real burden of existing debt, trigger cascading defaults, and risk a self-reinforcing debt-deflation spiral. Governments and central banks will not permit it for long. The historical response to such threats has been aggressive liquidity provision, fiscal stimulus, and monetary expansion - precisely the environment in which gold has thrived.
Warsh has little genuine choice. Like previous chairpersons, he must continue to do the unsustainable in order to sustain the unsustainable for a while longer. In a world of nearly USD40 trillion in debt, structurally large deficits, and politically sacred entitlement programs, the path of least immediate resistance is the one that tolerates higher inflation and a softer dollar.
Warsh, like Odysseus, appears to have chosen the less catastrophic path: sacrifice a few sailors (accept higher inflation and a weaker dollar) rather than risk the entire ship (a bond-market revolt that forces yield-curve control or worse).
At his recent press conference he talked tough about price stability, then left rates unchanged. The market’s response was telling - the 10-year yield pushed higher and the 30-year approached or exceeded 5.2 percent. Debt vigilantes read the decision as a signal that the Fed will ultimately prioritize financial stability and fiscal arithmetic over disinflation.
We are watching a modern Odysseus choose which sailors to feed to the monster. The ship may limp through the strait. The passengers holding real assets rather than paper promises are the ones most likely to reach the other side intact.

title: 美聯儲動輒得咎
text:
横又死，掂又死：美聯儲動輒得咎，在所難免
聯儲局主席凱文•沃什無論選擇哪條路，黃金都會勝出



在荷馬的《奧德賽》中，英雄奧德修斯必須駕船穿越一條狹窄的海峽，兩側各有致命危險。一邊是斯庫拉（Scylla），一頭有六顆腦袋的怪物，會從甲板上把水手抓走；另一邊是卡律布狄斯（Charybdis），一個巨大的漩渦，能把整艘船吞沒。女巫喀耳刻（Circe）建議他靠近斯庫拉航行，犧牲少數水手，也不要冒著整艘船被漩渦吞噬的風險。奧德修斯無奈照做，六名船員喪命，船卻得以倖存。
新任聯儲局主席凱文•沃什（Kevin Warsh）正處於同樣的海峽之中。一邊是大幅加息以壓制通脹；另一邊是維持低利率（或只小幅加息），任由通膨繼續侵蝕貨幣購買力。兩條路都係死路一條。唯一的問題是：他願意承受哪一種痛苦。
抑制通脹的直接辦法向來是提高利率。高利率會冷卻需求、支撐美元，最終讓物價受控。但美國身子虛弱，已不再是一個擔受得起這種經典療法的國家。目前全國總債務接近 39.8 兆美元，並有望在數月內突破 40 兆美元。本財年年度赤字接近 1.9 兆美元，且看不出有縮小的跡象。單是社會保障（Social Security）與聯邦醫療保險（Medicare）就佔聯邦預算極大比例 - 社會保障約佔支出的 22–23%，聯邦醫療保險另佔 14–17%。如今淨利息支出已相當於或甚至超過國防支出，並正朝每年超過 1 兆美元攀升。這些項目在政治上幾乎不可觸碰，尤其在中期選舉逼近之際。削減福利等於政治自殺。
加息也會重創股市。美國經濟高度依賴消費，而家庭財富以及消費信心與股價緊密相連。資本利得及相關稅收構成聯邦收入中不可忽視的一部分。股市若持續下跌，這些收入會縮水，同時利息成本卻在上升，進一步令財政狀況惡化。
然後是債券市場，真正的「房間裡的大象」。股市或許搶佔新聞頭條，但真正為政府融資的是美國公債市場。目前流通的美國公債已超過 30 兆美元；更廣泛的美國債券市場規模更大。長期殖利率上升會威脅整個國家的融資機制。當 10 年期美債殖利率從 2026 年 2 月底約 3.97% 升至現在 4.6% 或甚至更高時，政府（以及所有其他人）的借貸成本已明顯上升。如果沃什加息到足以殺死通脹的程度，將可能引發通縮式崩潰，而在目前的債務對 GDP 比率下，這在政治與經濟上都不可接受。物價與收入下跌會提高現有債務的實質負擔，觸發連鎖違約，並可能陷入自我強化的債務通縮螺旋，政府與央行不會長期容忍這種局面。歷史上政府對這類威脅的回應，一向是大規模注入流動性、財政刺激與貨幣擴張 - 而這正是黃金歷來蓬勃發展的環境。
沃什幾乎沒有真正的選擇。像之前的主席一樣，他必須繼續做不可持續的事，才能讓不可持續的局面再維持一陣子。在一個接近 40 兆美元債務、結構性龐大赤字、以及政治上被視為神聖不可侵犯的社會福利的世界裡，阻力最小的路徑就是容忍較高通脹與較弱美元。
沃什就像奧德修斯一樣，似乎選擇了傷害較小的那條路：犧牲少數水手（接受較高通脹與弱美元），也不願冒整艘船沉沒的風險（債券市場爆破，迫使實施收益率曲線控制或其他更糟措施）。在最近的記者會上，他對物價穩定說得強硬，卻選擇維持利率不變。市場的反應顯示長期殖利率將進一步走高，聯準會最終會優先考慮金融穩定而非通脹。
我們正看著一位現代奧德修斯，決定要把哪些水手餵給怪物。船或許能勉強穿過海峽，但最有可能安全抵達彼岸，是那些持有真實資產、而非紙上承諾的投資者。

title: 项庄舞剑
text:
项庄舞剑：贝森特真正在保卫的是日圆吗？
官方说法是援助盟友。真正的诱因，是防止美国国债市场出现失控式抛售。



秦朝末年，各路起义军中，刘邦与项羽的势力最为强大。双方曾约定：谁先攻下秦都咸阳，谁就在关中称王。结果刘邦先入咸阳，项羽大怒。
项羽的远房叔父项伯，与刘邦的谋士张良交情甚笃。听到消息后，项伯连夜赶去警告张良，劝他赶紧逃走。张良不愿抛弃主公，反而引荐刘邦与项伯相见。刘邦热情接待，并与项伯结为儿女亲家。项伯于是劝刘邦亲自前往向项羽解释、道歉。
翌日，刘邦率随从抵达鸿门。项羽的首席谋士范增力劝主公在宴席上除掉刘邦，并埋伏武士，约定项羽举杯为号即动手。
宴席上，刘邦态度谦卑、极尽奉承。项羽性情直爽，渐渐被安抚，不再有杀意，对范增多次示意皆视而不见。范增见计谋难成，便找来项羽的堂弟项庄，说：「大王太仁慈了。你进去以舞剑助兴为名，趁机杀了刘邦。」
项庄入席敬酒后，请求舞剑。剑光闪动，越舞越靠近刘邦。项伯见状着急，起身说：「一人独舞兴致不高，让我来对舞吧！」随即拔剑起舞，暗中以身体挡在刘邦身前，使项庄无法下手。
张良见情况危急，赶忙出去对刘邦的猛将樊哙说：「现在项庄拔剑起舞，他的用意就是要杀沛公啊！」这正是《史记》名句「今者项庄拔剑舞，其意常在沛公也」的由来。樊哙立即持武器闯入宴席。在张良与樊哙的保护下，刘邦最终找到机会离开，安全返回自己的军营。
这就是历史上著名的「鸿门宴」。
时光快转两千多年，场景换到华盛顿与东京。
美国财政部长斯科特•贝森特（Scott Bessent）刚刚与日本联手，罕见地进行协调干预，以支撑持续暴跌的日圆。官方说法是盟友之间的团结之举。日圆已跌至数十年低点，逼近1美元兑164日圆，为1980年代中期以来最弱水准。日圆此前处于无序贬值状态，进口通胀（尤其是能源与民生必需品）上升，东京担心日圆贬值陷入死亡螺旋。
表面上看，华盛顿的协助显得慷慨。但若进一步以「诱因是塑造人类行为最强力的力量」这条公理来分析，整出戏就像极了项庄舞剑：表面表演是一回事，真正的目标却是另一回事。
干预真正的目标，是防止美国国债出现失控式抛售。
日本是美国国债最大的外国持有者，帐上约持有1.14至1.2兆美元。若东京为了捍卫日圆而大量抛售这些国债，将在美国长期殖利率本已敏感的时刻，进一步推高殖利率。贝森特绝不会让这种情况发生。
干预日圆的逻辑十分明显。日圆贬值会把通膨输入日本。要支撑汇率，东京的选择有限。若积极加息，将推高日本政府公债殖利率。日本债务对GDP比率超过200%，殖利率急升可能引发经济衰退，并导致庞大的日圆套利交易（yen carry trade）无序平仓。
所谓日圆套利交易，是指借入低息日圆，投资于其他高收益资产，估计规模从数千亿美元到数兆美元不等（若计入杠杆与不列入资产负债表的部份）。日圆若突然大幅升值，这些套利交易就被迫平仓，投资者必须卖掉外国资产（包括美国国债）来偿还日圆借款，这是华盛顿最不想见到的情况。
日本的另一选择是卖出自己拥有的美国国债换取美元，再用美元买入日圆。贝森特不允许这种情况发生，因此他推动扩大联准会的「外国与国际货币当局回购机制」（FIMA Repo Facility）——目前每个交易对手每日上限为600亿美元——让日本能以国债作为抵押借入美元进行干预，而不必抛售美国债券。
在最近这次行动中，美国更进一步选择卖出欧元（而非美元）来买入日圆。若卖出美元，将与「强势美元」政策相矛盾，并可能进一步推高美国殖利率；卖出欧洲资产则无此顾虑。有报导指出，欧洲中央银行是在交易完成后才被告知——这是违背主要央行之间惯常咨商规范的罕见做法。
市场的即时反应相当戏剧性：日圆在短时间内急涨约5%。日圆升势持续了多久？数日后日圆就回吐相当部分涨幅，回落到1美元兑157至158日圆区间。历史经验显示，这类干预多半只是争取短暂喘息的时间，而非扭转根本趋势。利差、日本的财政轨迹，以及支撑日圆弱势的结构性力量，基本上都还在。若日圆贬值再度加速，将需要更大规模、更频繁的干预。
其他国家与大型机构也因各自理由（外汇储备管理、流动性、收益率等）持有大量美国债务。一旦其中任何一方因为某种需要——例如为了取得美元购买石油——而决定卖出美国国债，同样的压力就会出现。华盛顿不愿看到外国帐户在市场已承压时抛售美国国债，这将迫使贝森特发动越来越多此类干预。而这些干预，本质上不过是用凭空印出的美元，进行变相的收益率曲线控制。
简言之，为了不让美国长期国债殖利率升得太高、太快，贝森特会用尽一切可用方法以及任何必要手段，阻止美国国债泡沫爆破。
债券市场的损失，将被转移到货币层面，也就是我们口袋里的银纸购买力会不断下降。
对投资人而言，自保之路是黄金与白银。
项庄舞剑，嘴上说只是助兴。真正的意图，从来不是助兴。今天也一样。跟着诱因走，真正目的就清楚了。
